key_insight: Modern Mixture-of-Experts models can become less effective at exploring expert combinations when shared experts are added. The paper argues that routing should be rethought so that fine-grained expert segmentation still encourages diverse, useful expert selection instead of getting dominated by always-on shared experts.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the exploration dilemma in modern MoE architectures: how to preserve routing diversity and expert specialization when combining fine-grained expert segmentation with shared experts.
method: Analyzes the interaction between fine-grained expert segmentation and shared experts in modern MoE routing.
Identifies how shared experts can reduce routing exploration by making some paths too attractive or too stable.
Proposes a routing perspective that balances expressiveness, specialization, and exploration under a fixed activation budget.
impact: For practitioners, this work offers guidance for designing MoE systems that scale efficiently without sacrificing routing diversity or expert utilization. Better exploration can improve model capacity use, specialization, and overall performance in large-scale AI models.
visual_elements: Side-by-side MoE architecture diagram showing fine-grained experts vs. shared experts

paper_title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
paper_authors: Bingcong Li, Hao Ma, Michael Muehlebach, Niao He, Yi Ma
